diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac {(2\pi)^{\frac d2}}{t_2-t_1}  \mathbb E \Big[\operatorname{Arg} \Big(\Big|\frac {\widehat u(t_2, \xi)}{\widehat u(t_1, \xi)}\Big|\Big)\Big]& =\sum_{|\alpha|\le p_1, \alpha \; \text{odd}} a_{\alpha}(\bi \xi)^{\alpha}\bi^{-1}.

issues.failure_explanation: For any nonzero complex number z, Arg|z| = 0, so the displayed identities assert 0 = (nonzero odd-order polynomial in xi). The intended left-hand side is Arg of the ratio u_hat(t_2,xi)/u_hat(t_1,xi) itself (equivalently its imaginary part), whose expectation yields the odd drift coefficients; the same slip (plus a missing bi^{-1} factor in the subtracted drift term) is reproduced in the proof of Proposition prop:added-2. As written, the equations do not identify the odd-order drift coefficients.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the modulus inside Arg in mul-ide-2 and dri-mul-ide2 (and restore the missing bi^{-1} factor in the drift subtraction in by_odd of prop:added-2); the remainder of the argument is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The odd-order part of the drift identification in Proposition prop-drift-identification, and the pathwise uniqueness claim of Proposition prop:added-2 that reuses the same phase equation, are unsupported until the phase is taken of the ratio rather than of its modulus.
issues.title: Phase equation applies Arg to the modulus, zeroing the odd-drift identities
issues.why_classification: The erroneous displays are repaired by deleting the bars inside Arg (and one missing factor); the correction is forced, local, and preserves the identification conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
(\by_{odd})_k=\frac {2(2\pi)^{\frac d2}}{(t_2-t_1)} \log \frac {\mathbb E \widehat u(t_2, \xi_k)}
{\mathbb E \widehat u(t_1, \xi_k) }  -\sum_{|\alpha|\; \text{even}} a_{\alpha}(\bi\xi_k)^{\alpha}, k\le \widetilde K\;.

issues.failure_explanation: (a) The non-degeneracy hypothesis is imposed for hypersurfaces of degree <= 2p_1, but the regression matrices contain monomials xi^gamma with |gamma| <= 2p_2; when p_2 > p_1 the stated hypothesis does not imply full rank, so uniqueness is not supported (the forced correction, confirmed by the appendix, is degree <= 2p_2 with the explicit cardinality |Q_1| >= max(sum_{k<=p_2} C(2k+d-1,d-1), sum_{k<=p_2-1} C(2k+d,d))). (b) The polar-coordinate identities drop the factor (2pi)^{-d/2} relative to the exponential-moment display they are derived from. (c) by_odd is a copy of by_even: it uses log instead of Arg and subtracts the even-order a_alpha terms instead of the odd-order ones. (d) q_{\tilde\beta} appears in place of b_{\tilde\beta} in the appendix expansion. None of these affect the equivalence-class conclusion.

failure_location.quote: Assume that $|\mathcal Q_1|$ is sufficiently large and that $\mathcal Q_1$ is not located on an algebraic polynomial hypersurface of degree $\le 2p_1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the hypothesis to degree <= 2p_2 with the explicit cardinality given in the appendix; insert the missing (2pi)^{-d/2} factor; define by_odd with Arg and the odd-order a_alpha terms; replace q_{\tilde\beta} by b_{\tilde\beta}. All corrections are local.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness-up-to-equivalence conclusion survives, but as stated the rank hypothesis does not control the degree-2p_2 regression when p_2 > p_1, and the measurement vectors by_even/by_odd are misdefined, so the proof as written does not establish the claimed identifiability.
issues.title: Wrong hypersurface degree in the rank hypothesis and inconsistent algebra in the covariance-identification proof
issues.why_classification: All defects are local slips with forced corrections (degree 2p_2, explicit cardinality, one constant factor, the by_odd definition, b-typos); the equivalence-class identifiability conclusion survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that $-\mathcal L+\mu$ is admissible and that $u_0$ is $\mathcal F_0$-measurable  satisfying $|c_k|_{L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)}\le \theta k^{-\gamma}$ for some $\theta>0,\gamma>\frac 12.$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem promises a single fixed subspace V of H of dimension O(|log eps|^2) with the L^2(Omega;H) error O(eps), uniformly for t in [0,T]. At t=0, take deterministic c_k = theta k^{-gamma} (allowed by the hypotheses): u(0)=u_0 is deterministic and the best m-dimensional deterministic approximation error is sum_{k>m} theta^2 k^{-2gamma} ~ theta^2 m^{1-2gamma}/(2gamma-1), so accuracy eps requires m ~ eps^{-2/(2gamma-1)}, which is not O(|log eps|^2); the claim fails even allowing V to depend on t and on u_0. The proof never produces a fixed space: V_1 is spanned by vectors containing the random factors e^{q_k W(t)} and the possibly random c_k (and the additive-noise approximant w_epsilon^2 is built from stochastic integrals), i.e., the constructed spaces are path-dependent. Hence the argument establishes only a pathwise (random-space) version, not the stated fixed-space claim; the same defect affects the additive-noise item via the appendix proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair of the fixed-space statement exists: at minimum the theorem must be restated with V allowed to depend on the path/trajectory (the random space the proof constructs), which changes the central quantifier and guarantee type; the t=0 counterexample shows no repair of the statement as written can work.
issues.overall_effect: Both items of Theorem theorem-diffusion-identification (multiplicative and additive) are false as stated; the advertised logarithmic-dimensional 'averaged' approximation of the data space in the introduction, and the resulting parabolic-versus-hyperbolic difficulty comparison, lose their stated support.
issues.title: Data-space theorem is false as stated: no fixed O(|log eps|^2)-dimensional space can approximate u(0); the proof builds a path-dependent space
issues.why_classification: The stated fixed-space claim is false at t=0 under the theorem's own hypotheses, and the only source-supported resolution (path-dependent V) changes a central quantifier/guarantee type and abandons the advertised averaged low-dimensional data-space result.

issues.failure_explanation: For dX = -c(X) \circ dW with sigma(x) = -c(x), the Ito-Stratonovich correction is +1/2 sigma'(X)sigma(X) = +1/2 (partial_x c)(X) c(X), so the Ito form is dX = -c(X)dW + 1/2 (partial_x c)(X)c(X)dt. The displayed minus sign is wrong: for c(x)=x it yields X(0) e^{-W(t)-t/2} instead of geometric Brownian motion X(0) e^{-W(t)}. The downstream regularity claim X_{s,t} in C^p used later in the same proof is unaffected because it holds for either sign of the bounded drift.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of the correction term to +1/2 (partial_x c)(X) c(X) dt; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed Ito conversion in the proof of Lemma lem:added-1 is incorrect, but the lemma's conclusion and its later use of flow regularity survive.
issues.title: Sign error in the Ito form of the stochastic particle system
issues.why_classification: A one-sign correction with a forced verification (geometric Brownian motion check); the downstream regularity claim is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The differentiability of $G(s,t)$, i.e., $G(s,t)\in \mathcal C^{p}([0,T]^2)$ leads to 
$\lambda_j= o(j^{-(p+1)})$ (see, e.g., \cite{MR728689}).

issues.failure_explanation: The first equality is false in general: P_{V_K^k} and P_{V_G^k} project onto different spaces (leading eigenfunctions of the spatial kernel K(x,y) versus of the time kernel G(s,t)), and the two tails are sums of different eigenvalues, so they cannot be equated as displayed. The proof only establishes smoothness and eigenvalue decay for the time kernel G, while the conclusion ||u - P_{V_K^k}u||^2 = sum_{j>k} lambda_j needs the decay for the spatial kernel K. The conclusion is still correct and repairable: K(x,y) = int_0^T E[u_0(X_{s,0}^{-1} x) u_0(X_{s,0}^{-1} y)] ds is C^p because u_0 is C^p and the flow X_{s,0}^{-1} is C^p, giving lambda_j(K) = o(j^{-(p+1)}) and sum_{j>k} lambda_j(K) = o(k^{-p}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the display with the two separate tail identities and prove lambda_j(K)=o(j^{-(p+1)}) directly from the C^p regularity of K; the rest of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The dimension conclusion dim V = o(eps^{-2/p}) of Lemma lem:added-1 is correct but is not established by the argument as written; the hyperbolic data-space claim (and the prose comparison with the parabolic case) rests on this step.
issues.title: Invalid equality of space-kernel and time-kernel projection errors in the hyperbolic data-space lemma
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is standard and the repair (separate tail identities plus a direct C^p argument for K) is contained within the same lemma.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathbb E[u_{\widetilde M}(t,x)-u(t,x)]  =\sum_{k=\widetilde M+1}^{\infty} \mathbb E [c_k]e^{\bi\lambda_kt}e^{-\frac 12 q_k^2 t}\phi_k(x).

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition bounds the error for the deterministic vector E u(t) by a deterministic space V (E P_V u = P_V E u), and the proof itself correctly writes E[u_{\widetilde M}] with E[c_k]. But E[u_{M_epsilon}(t)] = sum_k E[c_k] e^{i lambda_k t} e^{-q_k^2 t/2} phi_k, not sum_k c_k e^{i lambda_k t} (truncated Taylor series); the displayed inequality pulls the random c_k through the expectation, discards the variance terms Var(c_k), and makes the approximating space V_t random. For random F_0-measurable c_k (allowed by the hypotheses), the stated deterministic-space conclusion is not established by the proof as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct w_epsilon and V_t with E[c_k] in place of c_k (using |E c_k| <= theta k^{-gamma}); every displayed estimate then goes through unchanged and V_t is deterministic.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop-dis's approximation statement for the mean trajectory is unproven for random initial data; the strong-data-space narrative in the introduction that relies on the contrast between mean and solution is unaffected in its (separately unsupported) strong part.
issues.title: Schroedinger weak data-space proof pulls random coefficients through the expectation
issues.why_classification: Replacing c_k by E c_k in w_epsilon and V_t is a local, forced repair that makes the space deterministic and validates every estimate; the logarithmic-dimension conclusion survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated bound is false. Taking bb = bb* with ||bb*|| large and ba != ba* small, S_diffuse(bb*|ba) = I^{-1} sum_i int |E[R_i^2(ba)] - E[R_i^2(ba*)]|^2 dx, and E[R_i^2(ba)] - E[R_i^2(ba*)] = sum_k (a_k - a_k*) E[ int_0^{t_i} F_k (2 R_i(ba*) + sum_{k'} (a_{k'}-a_{k'}^*) int F_{k'}) ] with R_i(ba*) = -int_0^{t_i} sum_j b_j* G_j dW. The cross term E[ int F_k int b*G dW ] is generically unbounded in ||bb*|| (e.g., for d u = a* u dt + b* u dW it grows like e^{(a*+b*^2)t}/(a*+b*^2)), so S_diffuse(bb*|ba) can be arbitrarily large while the stated bound stays O((||ba||+||ba*||)^2 ||ba-ba*||^2). The correct first factor is (||bb*||+||ba-ba*||)^2, coming from E|R_i(ba)|^2 <= C(||bb*||^2 + ||ba-ba*||^2). The displayed proof merely asserts the final inequality; it does not establish it. The lemma's intended use (the score is small when both coefficient vectors are accurate, justifying argmin model selection) survives the correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (||ba||+||ba*||)^2 by (||bb*||+||ba-ba*||)^2 in the first term and supply the missing estimate E|R_i(ba)|^2 <= C(||bb*||^2 + ||ba-ba*||^2); no change to the model-selection procedure is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative justification for selecting diffusion coefficients by minimizing S_diffuse is false as stated: the bound misses the dependence of the score on the magnitude of the true diffusion coefficients under drift misspecification, so the claimed bound can be violated by arbitrarily large factors.
issues.title: Model-selection score bound has a false drift-error factor
issues.why_classification: The stated inequality is genuinely false (not a typo) and requires redoing the estimate with the correct factor, but the repair is contained in one lemma and preserves the model-selection guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\bc^*$  is a local minimizer of $f_O$, by Theorem 5.1 of~\cite{vogel1994stochastic}, $f_N$ is lower semi-continuously convergent almost surely  to $f_O$ on the set $C_k := \{\bc:\|\bc\|=k\}$

issues.failure_explanation: As written, item 1 asserts that the optimal value of the deterministic problem eq_L0_drift_select_greedy (a constant) converges almost surely to the optimal value of eq_L0_drift_select_sample (a random variable), which is false in general. The content of the cited SA-convergence theory, and of item 2's limsup inclusion, is the reverse: the sample optimal value converges a.s. to the true optimal value. The intended statement is a forced swap of the two problems. (The proof additionally writes the constraint set as C_k = {bc : ||bc|| = k} instead of ||bc||_0 = k, and lsc convergence on the non-closed set {bc : ||bc||_0 = k} is asserted via the citation without any argument adapted to the l_0 constraint.)

failure_location.quote: \item  The optimal value of~\eqref{eq_L0_drift_select_greedy} converges almost surely to the optimal value of~\eqref{eq_L0_drift_select_sample}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Interchange the two problems in item 1: the optimal value of eq_L0_drift_select_sample converges a.s. to the optimal value of eq_L0_drift_select_greedy; also correct C_k to {bc : ||bc||_0 = k}.
issues.overall_effect: Item 1 of Theorem eq_convergence_theorem is false as stated; the asymptotic-consistency narrative for the drift estimator rests on the intended (reverse) direction.
issues.title: Sample-average convergence theorem states the optimal-value convergence backwards
issues.why_classification: The intended direction is the standard SA-convergence content supported by the proof of item 2, and the correction is a forced swap of the two problems.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Based on the almost surely convergent subsequence of minimizers specified in~\eqref{eq_Psi_def}, the asymptotic behavior of the surrogate~\eqref{eq_L0_diffuse_select_sample} can be similarly deduced.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem has no proof: the text only says the behavior 'can be similarly deduced'. The deduction is not immediate because the objective g_N(bc, ba) couples bc with a second argument ba that itself varies along a random subsequence ba_{N_k} -> ba, so one needs joint (epi-)convergence of g_N(.,.) on the non-closed constraint set {bc : ||bc||_0 = j}, which is neither argued nor cited for the coupled problem; additionally Phi_O is defined with g_O(bc, ba) instead of g_O(bc, bahat). The statement is plausible, but as a formal claim its guarantees (value convergence and the limsup inclusion of minimizers) are unsupported.

failure_location.quote: \item For any $\displaystyle \widehat{\ba}\in\limsup_{N\to\infty}\Psi_N$ as defined in~\eqref{eq_Psi_def}; that is,  there exists a subsequence $(\widehat{\ba}_{N_k})_{k=1}^\infty$  with $\widehat{\ba}_{N_k}\in \Psi_{N_k}$ that converges to $\widehat{\ba}$ almost surely, we have

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the joint epi-convergence argument for g_N(bc, ba_N) -> g_O(bc, ba) on the l_0 constraint set (or cite a result covering the coupled problem), and fix the Phi_O notation; the statement itself can stand.
issues.overall_effect: The almost-sure consistency of the diffusion coefficient estimator along convergent drift subsequences is claimed but not established; the model-selection guarantee built on these convergences is correspondingly unsupported.
issues.title: Diffuse sample-average convergence theorem is stated without proof
issues.why_classification: A necessary nontrivial argument (joint epi-convergence with a moving second argument) is missing entirely, but supplying the standard argument or a citation avoids any loss of the advertised guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The algorithm terminates when the regression error does not improve.

issues.failure_explanation: The loop breaks only when the residual sum of squares strictly increases; when it stays equal across an iteration (which can happen when the support changes without changing the objective value, or when the iterate stalls), the algorithm executes the Else branch, increments l, and continues, so it need not terminate. This contradicts the stated rule that the algorithm terminates when the regression error does not improve (non-improvement includes equality). The algorithm also contains no iteration cap; the 100-iteration cap exists only as an experimental setting.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Break on non-decrease (>=) of the residual sum of squares, or add an explicit iteration cap/stagnation tolerance inside the algorithm.
issues.overall_effect: QSP (Algorithm QSPalgo) can fail to terminate on stagnating iterates, and the implemented stopping rule is not the one the prose specifies; the candidate-generation output is unreliable in that regime.
issues.title: QSP termination rule fails on equal residuals and contradicts the stated stopping rule
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local change to the stopping rule (break on non-decrease or add a cap); the greedy selection guarantees are empirical in any case, so no substantive guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The decision rule is incomplete: the intermediate range Phi^{-1}(p*)/2 <= 2|Z_N| < Phi^{-1}(p*) (e.g., 0.82 <= 2|Z_N| < 1.64 for p* = 0.95) triggers neither decision, and for p* <= 1/2 the threshold Phi^{-1}(p*) <= 0 makes the rule vacuous. Moreover Z_N is standard normal under the null, so the statistic compared against the quantile should be |Z_N|, not 2|Z_N|; the factor 2 changes the actual size of the test away from the stated significance level.

failure_location.quote: Then for some significance level $p^* \in (0,1)$, we decide that the diffusion part contains multiplicative noise if $2|Z_N|\geq \Phi^{-1}(p^*)$, and it is only additive if $2|Z_N|<\Phi^{-1}(p^*)/2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Decide on |Z_N| against a single threshold Phi^{-1}(p*) with p* in (1/2, 1), assigning every value to one of the two decisions, and state the null distribution consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The shortcut that skips diffusion identification for detected additive noise can be triggered at the wrong rate or not at all for intermediate test statistics, so the computational-saving strategy is not implemented as specified.
issues.title: Additive-noise detection rule has an undefined decision region and a null-distribution mismatch
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local restatement of the thresholds with a consistent null distribution; the procedure remains heuristic either way, so no substantive guarantee is lost.
